title: Not for the Summer's Hour Alone
description: Not for the Summer's Hour Alone in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Lydia Sigourney wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 985 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Marriage Hymn”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Not for the sum-mer's hour a-lone, When skies re-splen-dent shine, And youth and plea-sure fill the throne, Our hearts and hands we join;

lines: Not for the summer's hour alone,
And youth and pleasure fill the throne,
Our hearts and hands we join;
But for those stern and wintry days
When Heaven's wise discipline doth make
Not for this span of life alone,
Which like a blast doth fly,
And as the transient flowers of grass,
But for a being without end
This vow of love we take;
Grant us, O God, one home at last,

licence: Public domain: Lydia Sigourney died in 1865.
credits: Words by Lydia Sigourney (1791–1865), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
